extracted.intended_audience: researchers (especially those new to reviewing) and others seeking formal training/certification as journal peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: A structured, self‑paced training course teaching the principles and practice of journal peer review, aimed at enabling researchers to accept and perform review requests with confidence and ethics. Covers models of peer review, how to read and critique manuscripts, writing reports, specialist considerations (statistics, methods), and post-review responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction to peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamentals of the peer review system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides grounding in what peer review is, its purpose in research quality control, and the general principles that underpin the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different peer review models
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding different models: single/double blind, open, transparent, post-publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the variants of peer review and their implications for anonymity, transparency, and reviewer behavior; helps reviewers adapt reports to the model used by a journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: The role of the reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibilities and ethics of the reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers duties such as providing timely, fair, and objective assessments; avoiding misuse of privileged information; declaring conflicts; and upholding research integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to get involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical steps for registering with journals and building a reviewer profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on finding opportunities to review, setting up profiles that showcase expertise, and networking with editors to become part of reviewer pools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considering review requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluating whether to accept a review based on expertise, time availability, and conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for deciding to accept: match of expertise to manuscript, sufficient time to provide a thorough review, absence of conflicts (personal, institutional, competitive), and steps to decline or suggest alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading the manuscript critically
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies for first-pass and detailed reading of a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques for efficiently triaging manuscripts (first-pass) and methods for in-depth critical appraisal (detailed reading), including tracking major vs minor issues and reproducibility cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying common issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Spotting methodological, ethical, and presentation problems in manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and indicators of common faults: flawed experimental design, statistical misuse, plagiarism or ethical omissions, unclear figures/tables, and poor structure or language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the review report
rubrics_metrics.description: How to structure the report, choose language, and make recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice on organizing reports (summary, major issues, minor points), using clear and constructive language, making actionable recommendations (accept/revise/reject), and supplying evidence for critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing different article types
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapting review approach for original research, reviews, and case studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights how expectations differ by article type (e.g., novelty and methods for original research; balance and comprehensiveness for reviews; clinical relevance and consent for case studies) and how to tailor assessment criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing review articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Special considerations when reviewing review/synthesis articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on scope, balance of literature coverage, methodology of synthesis, potential bias, accuracy of interpretation, and whether conclusions are supported by cited evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing methods/protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on reproducibility when reviewing methods and protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess completeness and clarity of methods, availability of data/code, sufficiency for replication, and adherence to reporting standards and protocol registries where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical review basics
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental statistical issues reviewers should flag for specialist review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies common statistical red flags (inappropriate tests, misuse of p-values, insufficient power, incorrect analyses) and guidance on when to recommend a dedicated statistical review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivering difficult feedback diplomatically and constructively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on maintaining a professional tone, focusing on evidence and suggestions for improvement, avoiding ad hominem or dismissive language, and fostering positive author–reviewer interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining confidentiality and adhering to ethical rules, including restrictions on AI tool use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules around not sharing manuscript content, not using unpublished results for personal gain, declaring ethical concerns, and specific notes on permissible/imperfect use of AI tools in reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: After the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibilities and options after submitting a review (revisions, post-publication, recognition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers follow-up duties such as evaluating revised manuscripts, responding to editor queries, post-publication commentary/corrections, and ways to gain recognition for reviewing (certification, reviewer credits).
